newsitem.title: UK: Oil price stable, China demand helps balance market.
newsitem.headline: Oil price stable, China demand helps balance market.

text.p: Oil prices meandered sideways on Monday in what traders said was a balanced market where rising crude supplies have been met by extra demand for oil products in the United States and China.
International bellwether North Sea Brent blend crude for June loading rose three cents by 1530 GMT to $18.30 a barrel.
Dealers said the return to full throttle of U.S. refining operations after spring maintenance has been easily countered by rising crude supplies.
And while European refiners still are finishing their round of seasonal repairs there is plenty of demand for crude outside the region.
"The market seems comfortable at about $18 a barrel," said a trader in London. "There's good demand in the U.S. and the Far East is shipping crude in from the Atlantic Basin. It's a balanced market."
Data released by Chinese customs on Friday showed that China has already imported in the first three months of this year nearly half the volume of oil products it purchased in 1996.

Dealers said China would probably be the main outlet for a huge heating oil and diesel buying spree by Singapore trading house Hin Leong, which has underpinned global refining margins in recent weeks.
The company has been responsible for purchases of around 17 million barrels since early March worth about $500 million, dealers said.
Asian refiners have bought record volumes of West African crude supplies for May to feed growing capacity in the region.
U.S. buyers are also competing for premium spot North Sea and West African cargoes to maximise gasoline production ahead of the summer driving season.
Fears of a lengthy disruption to Nigerian crude exports were extinguished on Monday when Anglo-Dutch oil giant Shell said it had resumed full operations of its Forcados blend.
Ethnic clashes forced Shell on Friday to reduce production by about 90,000 barrels per day (bpd), or some five percent of the OPEC member's average output.

Oil dealers said crude prices continued to find support from healthy refining margins, particularly in Asia where profits for regional benchmark have strayed not far from $5 a barrel for the past three months.
